messages:
Nia: Quick triage — onboarding lotus-int4 (compact table) shows extra invisible separators inside Japanese ruby (furigana) and flipped brackets in mixed he/zh samples. BLEU down ~6 on srt-multilang. Anyone seen invisible char insertions tied to quant tables? :thinking:

Hector: Can you paste the minimal repro and the quant flags? Is this tokenization or detokenization?

Nia: Repro: ```
./eval.py --model lotus-int4 --quant q4 --calib=per_channel --dataset srt-multilang --langs ja,he,zh --detok unicode --batch 12
```

Nia: Example: fp16 detok: "章フリガナ" (kanji+furigana). int4 detok: "章‌フリガナ" (U+200C ZWNJ inserted). Also he/zh sample shows brackets swapped around Hebrew fragment only in int4 output.

Jing: ZWNJ/U+200C insertion and bracket mirror suggest either normalization differences or a tokenmap collision. Dump the tokenizer bytes + token ids for the failing sample?

Nia: Dumped: ```
fp16 tokens: [0x5f20, 0x30d5, 0x30ea, 0x30ac, 0x30ca]
int4 tokens: [0x5f20, 0x200c, 0x30d5, 0x30ea, 0x30ac, 0x30ca]
# raw bytes show 0xE2 0x80 0x8C between E4 B8 B0 and E3 83 95 when other-script context present
```

eval-bot: Summary (srt-multilang subset): fp16 BLEU 39.4 chrF 0.601 | int4 BLEU 33.2 chrF 0.558 | delta BLEU -6.2

Hector: Try forcing tokenizer normalize to NFKC and `--preserve_whitespace=false` to narrow normalizer vs tokenmap. Also try regenerating the quant table with a different hash (xxh3) or salt.

Nia: Quick test: `--tokenizer-normalize=NFKC` removed the ZWNJ but BLEU still ~3 down. `--preserve_whitespace=false` removed NBSP cases but caused kana splits. Regenerating with `--quant-hash=xxh3 --quant-salt=7` on a test run now.

Jing: If hash/salt flips it, it's almost certainly an assignment collision. Add a regression sample (mixed ruby+RTL) to the onboarding smoke harness so future quant runs catch it.

Nia: Filed BUG-ml-2054 with repro, attached tokenmap_int4.json and failing sample set. Kicked off grid for hash/salt variants. Temporarily excluded lotus-int4 from auto-promote. Will update with which param fixes it.
